reviewer: Claude review of stored model labels, source records and mesh positions; not a radiologist review
decision: On 2026-11-18 the project owner asked for the 3D models to be bound.
rule: A stored model is bound to a structure requirement of one of its investigations when its own source label names the structure the requirement names, or one of the structures a combined requirement names, and the fidelity checker finds no conflict. A whole is not bound to a requirement that names its parts, and a part is not bound to its whole. A sided requirement needs a side stated by the label or the record that agrees with where the mesh lies, a mesh that lies on both sides of the midline, or, for a specimen of unrecorded side, the mirror-image assumption. Coverage is always partial.
method: The labels of all 142 models without a binding were compared with the names of the requirements of their investigations, family by family, against each source’s own label list. Where a label states a side, the stored mesh was decoded and its position compared with the midline of the same source, in the axes the source declares (“frames”). 108 bindings on 69 models were accepted. Each of the other 73 models is listed under “not_bound” with its reason.

evidence_values.own_word: the label and the requirement share the words that name the structure (term)
evidence_values.another_name: the label names the structure by another name, or by the abbreviation its source’s class list uses
evidence_values.kind_of: the label names something that is by definition a kind of what the requirement names

side_values.label_states_side: the label (or the source node name, side_quote) states this side or both, and the mesh lies there
side_values.record_states_side: the model record itself states the matching side
side_values.mesh_spans_both_sides: the label states no side, and the mesh lies on both sides of the midline
side_values.side_not_stated: neither the label nor the record states a side; bound on the mirror-image assumption
side_values.not_sided: the requirement has no left or right side

mirror_image_regions: Only the OpenEar ZETA temporal bone specimen rests on the mirror-image assumption: the source does not record which ear it is, and its axes are not registered to a patient.

hra-female-pelvis-v1.10-.why: glTF axes with Y up; the bladder meshes lie at greater Z than the rectum, sacrum and coccyx, so +Z is anterior and +X is the body’s left. The left ovary, tubes, ligaments, ureter and ilium meshes all lie at +X.

source-only-bp3d-sella-4.3-.why: BodyParts3D axes with Z up; the optic nerves run forward from the chiasm toward -Y, so -Y is anterior and +X is the body’s left. The pituitary gland marks the midline.

totalseg-v3-s0358-.why: RAS axes from the source sform: +X is the body’s right. The trachea marks the midline.

totalseg-v3-esophagus-s0358-.why: RAS axes from the source sform: +X is the body’s right. The thoracic vertebral bodies mark the midline.

nasalseg-p001-.why: LPS axes from the source NRRD header: +X is the body’s left. The nasopharynx marks the midline.

wt9fc-sub007-.why: RAS axes from the source sform: +X is the body’s right. The tongue is a midline organ; the mean of its four muscle meshes marks the midline.

hvsmr2-pat7-.why: RAS axes from the source sform: +X is the body’s right. No segmented structure marks the midline, so a label that states both sides must have separate connected parts at least the margin apart from left to right.

source_findings: HRA female pelvis v1.10: the meshes labelled right and left round ligament of uterus lie on the body’s left and right respectively, while every other sided mesh of the source (30, including both ilia, ovaries, tubes and ureters) lies on its labelled side. The round ligament labels are swapped in the source. Neither mesh is bound.

HRA female pelvis v1.10: the mesh labelled “Abdominal ostium of uterine tube” lies at the uterine cornua, with the same left-right extent as the cornua mesh, not at the fimbriated end of a tube. It is not bound.
HRA female pelvis v1.10: the bladder dome and bladder base meshes carry the same source label, “fundus of urinary bladder”. Neither is bound.
